title: Sorting, Classifying and Pictograms
seo_title: Sorting and Pictograms – Primary 1 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Sort and classify objects by colour, shape and size; count and record data; read simple pictograms. (summary of the NERDC Primary 1 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 1 maths worksheets on sorting and classifying objects, tally marks, picture graphs and simple bar graphs. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Sort things that are the same
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Sorting means putting things that are alike together, for example by colour, shape or size.
  • Count each group and write the number.
  • A picture graph shows how many in each group.

Examples

Example

Sort: red ball, blue ball, red cup

Red things: 2

Answer: 2 red, 1 blue

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Putting one thing in two groupsEach thing goes in one group.
Miscounting the picturesTouch each one once.
Reading the wrong rowFollow the row with your finger.

items.q: How many shapes are there in all?
items.e: Count each group: 2 hearts, 4 triangles, 5 circles. Then add: 2 + 4 + 5 = 11. (There are 3 groups, but the question asks for shapes.)
Count each group: 2 squares, 4 stars, 7 hearts. Then add: 2 + 4 + 7 = 13. (There are 3 groups, but the question asks for shapes.)
Count each group: 7 hearts, 3 circles, 5 stars. Then add: 7 + 3 + 5 = 15. (There are 3 groups, but the question asks for shapes.)
